newsitem.title: GERMANY: Sabena Germany seat capacity rises 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Sabena Germany seat capacity rises 30 pct.

text.p: Sabena said it has increased seat capacity between Belgium and Germany by 30 percent under its summer schedule effective March 30.
The Belgian national carrier said it now flies 324 times a week between Brussels and seven German airports using jet aircraft only.
Sabena has added a fourth daily flight to Berlin Tempelhof with Avro RJ85 and BAe 146 jets and a fourth daily service to Munich with Boeing 737-300 and 737-500 aircraft.
Flights to Duesseldorf and Hanover were upgraded to jet services earlier this year, a statement said.
On March 24 Swisscargo said it is winning market share in Germany thanks to the additional freight capacity of Sabena.

The airline's general cargo manager Germany, Ulf Steinmann, told Reuters in an interview that 25 percent more freight capacity and access to Sabena's Brussels hub should boost Swissair cargo sales strongly this year.
Swisscargo took over global sales and marketing of Sabena's freight on January 1 this year as part of the Swiss airline's operational takeover of the Belgian carrier.
Since March 1, Swissair was thus routeing European airfreight via Brussels to use the quick turnaround times at the Belgian airport, he explained.
Steinmann said he planned to carry 25,000 tonnes of German freight this year compared to 21,000 tonnes in 1996.
About 80 percent of this is trucked to Zurich or Brussels for onward air transportation, he noted. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax: 5017
